about.title: About Me
bio: I'm a Tech Lead specialized in fintech payment platforms and multi-tenant systems.
I've built and scaled payment infrastructure across Latin American markets.
I've led teams of 5+ engineers with a focus on event-driven architecture, clean architecture, and CI/CD automation using TypeScript, Python, PostgreSQL, Azure, and AWS.
I care about shipping reliable software — and about the tooling, pipelines, and code review culture that make teams faster.

cards.title: Loopay Suite
cards.summary: Multi-tenant, cloud-native fintech payments platform for Latin American markets.
bullets: Lead a team of 5 engineers — architecture decisions, code reviews, and production support (NestJS, React, PostgreSQL, Azure, Terraform).

Lead SOBERANA, the cross-border payments platform: custodial wallets, virtual accounts, and payouts through external providers behind Strategy and Adapter patterns, so adding a provider does not change the core.

Led the AWS-to-Azure migration with the CTO, rebuilding the infrastructure in Terraform with GitHub Actions CI/CD over OIDC (no stored cloud credentials) and an ephemeral environment per pull request.
Built LoopayOCR, compliance document management with Google Gemini OCR, dynamic Pydantic schema validation, S3 storage, and webhook notifications.

cards.title: Galgo
cards.summary: Motorcycle e-commerce with embedded financing in Colombia.
bullets: Worked on the Checkout and Risk teams building NestJS backend services, a backend-for-frontend (BFF) layer, and Next.js interfaces on event-driven microservices (AWS).
Maintained systems on the critical path of checkout and risk evaluation, with cloud infrastructure and observability through Terraform, Datadog, and GitHub Actions.

cards.title: Trebet
cards.summary: Mobile super-app for residential communities — payments, digital intercom, amenity bookings, and assembly voting, with real-time built on WebRTC and WebSockets.
bullets: Co-founded the startup and built it with a remote team of 7 across Colombia, Mexico, and Venezuela.
Took the MVP to production in about a month — mobile app, backend services, and infrastructure (React Native, Laravel, DigitalOcean).
Moved the infrastructure from AWS to DigitalOcean when funding ran out, migrating the database ahead of the DNS cutover with no data loss.
